value.text: Audit 2026-09-13: EXISTS — engine/transport.ts implements the Phase 3 transport with FileTransport, push/pull, capability negotiation, and object transfer. value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Design for the served repository, reusing engine/transport.ts rather than forking it. The Transport interface stays the single boundary: its methods become async (a wire is asynchronous, a filesystem is not, and the interface was written so the algorithm does not care), FileTransport keeps every policy - fast-forward, force, compare-and-swap publication, verified arrival - and the HTTP server delegates every repository operation to a FileTransport opened on the repository directory under --root. Wire: POST <base>/advertise|fetch|push|objects/missing|objects/upload|publish, JSON envelopes with base64 payloads, error body {code,message} mapped back to ObjectStoreError so refusals read identically to a file remote. Client: HttpTransport implements the same interface, so clone/fetch/push/remote-add work unchanged through openTransport; the bearer token travels in the remote URL's userinfo. Resumable uploads keep their connection identity: the server holds one FileTransport per upload session, so publish reports exactly what that session delivered. Series and review records ride the same object paths: records are tree-reachable, series objects transfer through the verified-arrival upload path. Tenancy: bearer tokens scoped per repository (read/write); every pre-authorization failure - missing repo, wrong tenant, bad token, path traversal - answers with one byte-identical 404 denial; body sizes, object counts and session counts are bounded.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: PR #91 review follow-up (Greptile comments 4182612126 and 4182612135), resumed as pi-glm. P1: pushTo reads each tracking ref's expected value after the awaited push, so a late HTTP answer can overwrite a newer tip another fetch or push recorded while the wire was busy — capture the tracking values before sending and apply them only as compare-and-swap, moving a tracking ref past the captured value only when the pushed commit descends from it and never backward. P2: upload sessions have per-request bounds only, so one write session can accumulate fresh hash-valid blobs' receipts without end and reuse keeps it from evicting — add cumulative per-session object-count and byte bounds to ServeLimits (configurable, sane defaults, documented in README), refuse past them with the existing limit_exceeded shape, and release the session's receipts with the refusal. Planning a real-socket concurrency test for the late push and an adversarial session-bound test.

value.author: pi-glm
value.text: Implementation landed in the worktree: (1) pushTo now captures each tracking ref before the push leaves and, on the late answer, applies it only as a compare-and-swap against the captured value — advancing forward when the pushed commit descends from the ref's current value and skipping otherwise, so a tip another fetch or push recorded during the flight is never overwritten backward. (2) ServeLimits gains cumulative per-session bounds maxSessionObjects (default 1,000,000) and maxSessionBytes (default 4 GiB), both configurable via ServeOptions and validated like the other bounds; an upload past either is refused with the existing limit_exceeded shape and the session's receipts are released with the session, and publication clears the charge with the receipts on every attempt. (3) startRepositoryServer accepts an optional ServeHooks.holdResponse observability hook, invoked after a request's outcome is decided and before the response is written, which the concurrency test uses to hold a real push answer in flight. Tests: a real-socket concurrent case (server accepts A, a second client pushes B, the pusher fetches B, then A's answer completes — tracking keeps B), a held-answer file-transport case covering recorded/advanced/deleted-during-flight branches, and an adversarial session-bound test driving per-request-legal uploads past both the object and byte bounds and proving the refusal released the receipts.
